claims.text: Single-phase equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low yield strength.
Single-phase equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low hardness.
The low hardness and strength are caused by the absence of nanoscale chemical clusters or short-range order.
The starting equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is a homogeneous simple solid solution lacking nanoscale clusters and short-range-ordered regions.
A solution treatment near 1100 °C will homogenize CoCrFeNiTi.
Aging solution-treated CoCrFeNiTi at 500–600 °C for up to 10 hours will induce nanoscale chemical clustering or short-range order.
Nanoscale clusters or short-range-ordered regions impede dislocation glide by acting as pinning obstacles.
The induced obstacles force dislocations to pile up.
Dislocation pinning and pile-ups increase work hardening and shift the yield point upward.
The aged CoCrFeNiTi alloy will have greater tensile and compressive yield strength than the solution-treated control.
The aged CoCrFeNiTi alloy will have greater hardness than the solution-treated control.
The aged CoCrFeNiTi alloy will exhibit a higher work-hardening rate than the solution-treated control.
The continuous matrix will allow the aged alloy to retain good ductility despite strengthening.
The aged alloy will retain good machinability.
TEM or APT will reveal aging-induced nanoscale clusters or short-range order whose occurrence correlates with the mechanical improvements.
The controlled comparison uses nominally equimolar CoCrFeNiTi from the same batch, with a solution-treated control and an otherwise identically treated aged group.
The hypothesis is limited to equimolar CoCrFeNiTi within ±5 at.% compositional tolerances, aging at 500–600 °C for no more than 10 hours, and mechanical testing at temperatures no higher than 600 °C.

contradictions.description: The control is alternately described as as-cast, solution-treated, and 'as-cast (solutionized only).' As-cast and solution-treated are distinct processing states, so the actual baseline is internally ambiguous.

The falsification rule requires both no strengthening and no detectable clusters. Failure to form clusters would demonstrate failure of the intervention to create the proposed mediator, not falsify the claim that clusters strengthen the alloy. A more decisive falsifier would be formation of quantified clusters without the predicted strengthening.
